purpose: Stage 3A dynamic-execution gate: distinguish unsafe/unresolved dynamic execution from pre-existing, allowlisted jsdom test-harness eval. Counts are reported at the granularity that is actually true -- static site count vs. reachable invocation count -- not conflated into one number.

allowlistedEntries.mechanism: dom.window.eval(src) -- jsdom window-context eval, NOT Node vm/eval/new Function on arbitrary source
allowlistedEntries.staticallyReachableInvocationCountNote: buildEnv() has 19 call sites across the file (one per test scenario that needs a DOM+eval environment). Presented honestly as a static reachability count, not conflated with a measured runtime execution count (this script has not been executed).

srcSources.resolutionFunction: readMaybeMutated(relPath, useMutated, transform) (line 315), get = (rel) => readMaybeMutated(rel, !!mutations[rel], mutations[rel]) (line 365)
srcSources.externalInputControl: NONE -- the 9-entry array is a hardcoded literal in source; argv/env/network/user input cannot add, remove, or reorder entries, and cannot substitute a different path for any entry. This fixed, trusted, no-external-input allowlist is the actual safety boundary for this eval call -- not a claim about jsdom sandbox strength (see below).

jsdomConstructionOptions.resources: not set (jsdom default: no external resource loading)

allowlistedEntries.jsdomSandboxClaim: IMPORTANT: this evidence does NOT claim jsdom provides a safe sandbox for executing untrusted code. jsdom is a DOM implementation, not a security sandbox, and running arbitrary/untrusted script through dom.window.eval() would not be safe regardless of these options. The actual and only safety property being claimed here is narrower: the source text passed to eval() always originates from the fixed 9-file allowlist above (verified/mutated copies of those exact files only), so the question of jsdom's sandbox strength against a malicious payload does not arise in this harness -- there is no untrusted-input path into eval() at all.

nodeCapabilitiesExposedToEvalContext.note: grep-confirmed: no dom.window.require, dom.window.process, or dom.window.fs assignment anywhere in this file. This absence-of-explicit-injection check proves jsdom's own default globals were not supplemented with Node capabilities by this test file -- it does NOT by itself prove jsdom internals expose nothing sensitive; it is one supporting data point, not the primary safety argument (the primary argument is the fixed source allowlist above).
